editorialNote: First flagship research edition. Market data as at Friday 13 November 2026 close where available. Research candidates are not buy recommendations; no unverified valuation multiples or price targets are shown.

cards.title: Higher-for-longer rates meet an AI leadership shock
cards.dek: Inflation is proving sticky, yields are elevated and NVIDIA's CEO departure has unsettled the AI trade. The opportunity is shifting toward businesses that can prove cash returns on capital.
cards.insight: Our base case is selective risk-off, not the end of the AI investment cycle. The market is demanding stronger evidence that capital expenditure converts into recurring earnings and free cash flow.
cards.whyItMatters: Higher discount rates pressure long-duration equities, property and leveraged balance sheets. AI capex needs to be judged against incremental revenue, margins and cash generation.
cards.investmentOpportunity: Watch quality compounders with measurable cash conversion, copper exposure with mid-cycle discipline, and infrastructure businesses with contracted demand. Avoid treating one-session sector moves as durable rotation.

cards.title: BHP: copper scale, but don't capitalise peak prices
cards.dek: Copper contributed more than half of BHP's FY26 underlying EBITDA for the first time. The long-term demand case is compelling, but September-quarter production fell 19% year on year.
cards.insight: BHP offers diversified exposure to copper's structural demand story with a large, cash-generative iron ore business. The key distinction is that higher realised copper prices have supported recent earnings while production faced grade and maintenance headwinds.
cards.whyItMatters: A sustained copper supply deficit could support earnings and project returns. But extrapolating spot prices into terminal earnings risks overpaying at the top of the cycle.
cards.investmentOpportunity: Research at mid-cycle copper and iron ore prices; stress-test lower prices, production delays, capex and costs. Watch the copper production recovery and Jansen delivery. Thesis breaks if operational reliability deteriorates or capital returns fall below the cost of capital.
cards.source: BHP FY26 results · Q1 FY27 operational review

cards.title: Goodman: scarce power and land meet AI infrastructure
cards.dek: FY26 operating earnings per security rose 10.1%, with data centres accounting for 78% of the A$19.7bn development work-in-progress pipeline.
cards.insight: Goodman's advantage is not simply exposure to data-centre demand. Secured power, scarce urban land, customer relationships and development capability may support attractive project economics.
cards.whyItMatters: The same higher bond yields that pressure property valuations can reduce the equity value of long-duration development earnings. Strong operating growth alone does not settle the valuation question.
cards.investmentOpportunity: Compare price with operating earnings, NTA and development yields. Stress-test discount rates, construction costs, power delivery and leasing. Thesis breaks if yields compress, projects slip or occupancy weakens.

cards.title: CSL: the recovery case now has an earnings hurdle
cards.dek: After a difficult FY26 reset, CSL expects FY27 revenue broadly in line with the prior year and underlying NPAT growth of approximately 5%.
cards.insight: CSL retains valuable plasma and specialty medicines franchises, but the investment case has shifted from quality at any price to proof of execution. The FY27 growth target is the first measurable checkpoint.
cards.whyItMatters: A turnaround can create upside if margins normalise and newer therapies scale, but a low headline valuation may simply reflect a lower sustainable earnings base.
cards.investmentOpportunity: Value on normalised underlying earnings and free cash flow; exclude one-off charges but scrutinise recurring costs. Watch plasma economics, Seqirus demand, Vifor declines and transformation delivery. Thesis breaks if guidance is missed or core plasma economics deteriorate.

cards.title: Alphabet: AI is accelerating Cloud, but capex is the test
cards.dek: Q3 revenue rose 25% and Google Cloud grew 103%. The market must now judge whether enormous infrastructure spending earns attractive incremental returns.
cards.insight: Alphabet has multiple routes to monetise AI across Search, Cloud and subscriptions. Search query growth and Cloud acceleration show demand, but capex and depreciation will increasingly determine the quality of that growth.
cards.whyItMatters: Revenue growth can coexist with weaker free cash flow if infrastructure investment grows faster than monetisation. The key metric is return on incremental capital, not AI user counts alone.
cards.investmentOpportunity: Assess Search durability, Cloud margin progression and owner earnings after capex. Use a sum-of-the-parts framework with downside cases for AI search disruption and infrastructure returns. Thesis breaks if Search monetisation weakens or Cloud growth fails to translate into cash.

cards.title: Microsoft: enterprise distribution is the moat
cards.dek: FY26 revenue rose 18% to US$331.8bn and operating income rose 21%. The next question is how much incremental profit AI can deliver after infrastructure costs.
cards.insight: Microsoft's enterprise relationships and cloud ecosystem give it several paths to monetise AI. The reported EPS growth includes discrete benefits, including investment gains, so recurring operating earnings deserve the focus.
cards.whyItMatters: A premium business can still be a poor investment if its valuation assumes AI economics that are not yet visible in free cash flow per share.
cards.investmentOpportunity: Track Azure growth, paid Copilot adoption, operating margins and capex relative to operating cash flow. Normalise one-off investment gains. Thesis breaks if cloud growth slows, AI attach rates disappoint or capital intensity compresses returns.

cards.title: Amazon: AWS acceleration versus a cash-flow bill
cards.dek: AWS sales grew 39% and operating income reached US$17.8bn, but 2026 capex is expected to be about US$220bn and free cash flow has come under severe pressure.
cards.insight: AWS is a powerful growth engine and retail operating leverage is improving. But the scale of investment means the equity story increasingly depends on future cash returns rather than near-term revenue acceleration.
cards.whyItMatters: If data-centre assets generate strong returns, today's capex can build a durable earnings base. If utilisation, pricing or useful lives disappoint, depreciation and financing costs can absorb much of the growth.
cards.investmentOpportunity: Model AWS separately and stress-test incremental return on infrastructure capital, depreciation and free cash flow recovery. Thesis breaks if AWS growth decelerates while capex remains elevated and cash conversion fails to recover.

cards.title: NVIDIA: founder succession adds a new risk premium
cards.dek: Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO is confirmed. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor.
cards.insight: This is a company-specific leadership and governance shock with potential implications for customer relationships and US-China chip policy. It is not proof that AI demand has ended.
cards.whyItMatters: NVIDIA's founder has been central to product strategy and the AI ecosystem. The market must reassess succession, board oversight and strategic continuity.
cards.investmentOpportunity: Keep NVIDIA on a watchlist, not the initial Conviction List. Monitor official board updates, succession clarity, customer commitments and export-policy implications. Do not treat unverified espionage allegations as established fact.
